pod: Techniques of Improvement and Administrative Reform
blurb: Paper I asks about the tools — O&M, MIS, network analysis, e-governance — almost every year, usually as a 10-marker. Paper II asks why the reforms those tools were meant to serve were never implemented. India's answer: it reformed processes, not structures.

items.d: **Work study** seeks efficiency in **method** — how a specific task is done. **Organisation and methods** seeks efficiency in **structure and procedure** — how work flows between posts and units. The first optimises a step; the second asks whether the step should exist.

items.t: The two halves of work study
items.d: **Method study** — recording and critically examining the existing method to develop an easier, more economical one (process charts, flow diagrams, the **questioning technique**: purpose, place, sequence, person, means). **Work measurement** — establishing the **standard time** for a qualified worker, through time study, activity sampling or synthesis.

**2019 Q8(b).** **Staffing norms** grounded in measurement rather than precedent; **elimination of redundant steps**; **standardised procedure** that makes training and audit possible; and a **baseline** against which any later improvement can be proved. It is the only technique that produces a **defensible number** for how many staff a task needs.

The **O&M Division** in the **Cabinet Secretariat (1954)**, created on **Appleby's** recommendation, moved to the **Department of Administrative Reforms (1964)**, now **DARPG**. The **Staff Inspection Unit (1964)** in the Ministry of Finance fixes **staffing norms** for Union offices by work measurement.

**2025 Q7(c).** GPR asks the question work study does not: **should this process exist at all?** It **redesigns from the outcome backwards** rather than optimising existing steps. The **2nd ARC's 11th Report (Promoting e-Governance)** insisted GPR must **precede** computerisation — otherwise you **automate an unnecessary procedure**.

**Faceless assessment and appeal** in income tax abolished the **jurisdiction-based officer-taxpayer interface** rather than digitising it. **Passport Seva** redesigned the whole application chain around a **single visit**. **Self-attestation** replacing attestation by a gazetted officer removed a step entirely — the purest GPR of all, and free.

**SCDPM (DARPG)**, run annually — **record weeding, space released, files closed, pending references disposed, scrap disposal revenue**. It is **O&M in contemporary form**: unglamorous, measurable, and the kind of housekeeping that determines whether a department can find anything.

items.t: Where the technique reaches its limit
items.d: Work study can tell you the **standard time** for issuing a certificate. It cannot tell you whether the certificate should be **required**, whether the applicant should have to appear, or who should bear the cost of the visit. **Efficiency questions cannot answer purpose questions** — Taylor's original blind spot.

**PERT (US Navy Polaris, 1958)** — **probabilistic**, event-oriented, for projects whose activity times are **uncertain**, using **optimistic, most likely and pessimistic** estimates in a weighted formula. **CPM (DuPont, 1957)** — **deterministic**, activity-oriented, for **repetitive** projects with known times, and it costs the time-cost trade-off.

**2024 Q5(c).** The **longest path** through the network, and therefore the **shortest possible project duration**. Activities on it have **zero float** — delay any one and the whole project slips. Everything off it has **slack**, which is where resources can be borrowed from without cost.

**Crashing** = shortening a **critical** activity by adding resources. CPM's value is that it shows **which** activity to crash for the least cost per day saved — the only rational basis for spending money to accelerate a project rather than spending it everywhere.

items.t: What network techniques give an administrator
items.d: A **defensible schedule**, a clear view of **which delay actually matters**, a basis for **resource levelling**, and **accountability by activity** rather than by project. **PM Gati Shakti's** integrated planning and **PRAGATI's** project reviews both rest on this logic.

items.t: Why networks do not remove delay
items.d: **2019-family question, and 2025 Q8(c) on management aid tools.** A network **schedules activity**; it cannot resolve the **uncertainty** that causes delay — land acquisition, forest clearance, litigation, contractor default, fund release. It **makes the delay visible and attributable**, which is valuable, and is often mistaken for preventing it.

items.t: The efficacy of management aid tools
items.d: **2025 Q8(c).** State the governing principle: a tool's value depends on **fit between the tool and the problem**. Use **CPM** for a defined project with known steps; **PERT** where durations are uncertain; **cost-benefit** for choosing between alternatives; **MIS** for continuous control. Applying the wrong one produces **precision without relevance**.

items.t: The other aid tools worth naming
items.d: **Gantt chart** (bar schedule, no dependencies); **Management by Objectives (Drucker)**; **operations research** and linear programming; **queueing theory** for counter design; **decision trees**; **simulation**; **balanced scorecard** for multi-dimensional performance. Name two that fit; do not list.

An **integrated system** that converts data from internal and external sources into **information**, delivered at the **right level, in the right form, at the right time**, to support **planning, control and decision-making**. Note the emphasis: not data storage but **decision support**.

**Transaction processing** at the bottom (routine, detailed, operational); **MIS** in the middle (summarised, exception-based, tactical); **decision support and executive information systems** at the top (aggregated, ad hoc, strategic). Sending **operational detail to the top** is the commonest design failure.

**2019 Q5(d) — 'a narrow view of information'.** The system is built for **upward reporting** rather than for the **level that acts**; data is **entered but not used**, so quality decays; there is **no process redesign** alongside; and **fear of exposure** produces defensive reporting. **Garbage in, gospel out.**

items.t: MIS's evolution beyond its traditional role
items.d: **2021 Q5(e) and 2023 Q5(b).** It has moved from **periodic reports** to **real-time dashboards**, from **internal** data to **integrated external** feeds, from **descriptive** to **predictive** analytics, and from **specialist** access to **public** access — **data.gov.in**, the **NDAP**, scheme dashboards.

items.t: Indian MIS that carry real weight
items.d: **PFMS** — tracking every release to the beneficiary; **NREGASoft** with muster rolls online; **CCTNS** linking police stations; **e-Hospital and ABDM**; **UDISE+** for schools; **PRAGATI** with geo-tagged project data; **National Judicial Data Grid** making pendency publicly visible.

**2023 Q5(b).** It adds value by **shortening the decision cycle**, **exposing exceptions** rather than reporting everything, **standardising definitions** so units can be compared, and **making performance visible** — which is also why it meets resistance from the units it renders visible.

A live warning. When the **dashboard becomes the object**, staff optimise the **entry** rather than the **service** — Goodhart's law again. The safeguard is **third-party verification**, **outcome rather than output indicators**, and **beneficiary-side data** (call-back surveys, social audit) that the reporting unit does not control.

**G2C** (citizen services — passports, DBT, land records), **G2B** (business — GeM, single-window clearance, GST), **G2G** (inter-government — e-Office, PFMS, treasury), **G2E** (employees — iGOT, e-HRMS). Sorting a question into one of these four is the fastest way to structure the answer.

**Broadcasting** (information dissemination); **critical flow** (targeted release of critical information to those who can act); **comparative analysis** (benchmarking against best practice); **e-advocacy or mobilisation and lobbying** (networked civil action); **interactive service** delivery. **2025 Q5(a) asked about the e-advocacy model.**

**2025 Q5(a).** It **lowers the cost of collective action** — online consultation on **MyGov**, campaign mobilisation, crowdsourced evidence, RTI data used publicly. Its limits: the **digitally connected are not representative**, so it can **amplify already-heard voices**, and **manufactured consensus** is cheap.

**Presence** (a website) → **interaction** (downloadable forms) → **transaction** (payment and delivery end-to-end) → **transformation** (integrated, seamless, life-event-organised) → **engagement** (co-production and open data). India's variance across departments spans **all five stages simultaneously** — Riggs's heterogeneity, digitally.

**NICNET (1987)** → **National e-Governance Plan (2006)** with mission-mode projects and the **CSC** last mile → **Digital India (2015)** with its nine pillars → **India Stack and Digital Public Infrastructure**. The shift is from **departmental computerisation** to **shared population-scale rails**.

**2019 Q5(e).** **Partly.** It removed **discretion at the interface** — faceless assessment, online allotment — and **flattened information access**. It did **not** flatten hierarchy: approvals still climb the same levels, now in **e-Office**. It **relocated** bureaucratic power to whoever **designs the workflow and owns the data**.

**2020 Q8(a), 2024 Q6(b).** What changed the contours: **mobile-first** rather than desktop; **cloud** (MeghRaj) removing per-department infrastructure; **API-based interoperability** rather than monolithic systems; **real-time payments**; and **AI/ML** moving from analysis to **decision support**.

The necessary counterweight. **Connectivity and device access** are unequal; **digital literacy** more so; **authentication failure** excludes the elderly and manual workers; **language** narrows reach — which **Bhashini** addresses; and **assisted access through CSCs** reintroduces an **intermediary** with the discretion the system was meant to remove.

items.t: Cyber security as an administrative problem
items.d: **2025 Q5(c) asked about low cyber awareness.** The vulnerability is **behavioural, not technical** — phishing, shared credentials, unpatched systems, personal devices on official work. Instruments: **CERT-In** directions, **CISO** in every ministry, **cyber crisis management plans**, the **National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre**, and mandatory **iGOT** cyber-hygiene modules.

**Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023**, **Rules 2025** — consent, purpose limitation, a **Data Protection Board**, and **significant data fiduciary** obligations. Every department is now a **data fiduciary**: it needs a grievance officer, breach notification, and a lawful basis for processing. **Puttaswamy (2017)** is the constitutional root.

groups.g: Digital public infrastructure and the 2026 frontier

items.d: **Interoperable, open, population-scale digital rails** on which both government and private services are built — **identity, payments and data exchange** as public goods rather than departmental assets. Its administrative significance is **reuse**: one rail, many services, no rebuilding.

**Identity** — Aadhaar, e-KYC, e-Sign, **140 crore+ enrolments**. **Payments** — UPI, **20 billion+ monthly transactions** at 2025-26 peaks and **80%+** of retail digital payment volume. **Data empowerment** — DigiLocker (**45 crore+ users**), Account Aggregator, consent artefacts. **Commerce** — ONDC. **Language** — Bhashini.

**2023 Q3(a) asked exactly this.** It **advanced development goals** (DBT reaching the beneficiary directly), **raised public sector efficiency** (authentication and payment as a shared service), and **unlocked private innovation** (fintech built on UPI). Frame it as **Dunleavy's reintegration and needs-based holism** delivered at scale.

**2025 Q6(b).** **For** — deduplication, portability of entitlement, DBT at scale, financial inclusion through JAM. **Against** — **authentication failure and exclusion**, function creep beyond the original purpose, and privacy. **Puttaswamy (2018)** upheld it for **subsidies and taxation** under a law, and struck down **Section 57**'s private-party mandate.

**2025 Q6(a).** A public procurement marketplace producing **price discovery, transparency and MSME participation**. Its implementation problems: **specification gaming** to favour a supplier, **quality assurance** at the point of receipt, **payment delays** to sellers, **seller verification and counterfeits**, and **State adoption** that remains uneven.

**2023 Q7(c) asked it in Paper I; 2025 Q8(c) in Paper II.** Live uses: **grievance routing on CPGRAMS**, **judicial translation (SUVAS) and transcription**, **crop-yield and flood forecasting**, **GST fraud analytics**, **faceless assessment allocation**, and **Bhashini** for multilingual delivery.

items.t: The administrative case against unexamined AI
items.d: The 2026 argument to have ready. **Opacity** — a citizen cannot be told why a claim was rejected, defeating the **reasoned order** requirement. **Bias** — trained on historical data, it reproduces historical exclusion. **Accountability** — **who is the officer** when the model decides? The answer must be that **AI advises and a named official decides**.

**IndiaAI Mission**; **NITI's Responsible AI for All** principles (safety, equality, inclusivity, privacy, transparency, accountability); **DPDP Act** obligations on the training data; **sectoral regulators** (RBI on model risk, SEBI on algo-trading). India's stated position is **pro-innovation regulation** rather than a single horizontal AI Act.

groups.g: Administrative reform — theory and the Indian record

items.d: **2020 Q7(c) quoted it.** Administrative reform is "**the artificial inducement of administrative transformation against resistance**." Every word is doing work: **artificial** (deliberate, not evolutionary), **transformation** (not adjustment), and **against resistance** — resistance is **constitutive**, not an obstacle that competent design avoids.

**Interest-based** — the reform removes someone's discretion, rent or status. **Cognitive** — officials cannot see how the new way would work. **Cultural** — the change conflicts with the organisation's self-image. **Structural** — statutes, service rules and federal division make the change legally slow.

**Political sponsorship at the highest level** — no reform survives without it; **a compelling crisis or trigger**; **compensation for the losers** (redeployment, protected pay); **early visible wins**; **legal backing** so the change survives a transfer; and **a champion who remains in post** long enough to see it through.

**Secretariat Reorganisation (N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, 1949)**; **Gorwala (1951)** on integrity; **Appleby (1953, 1956)**; **Santhanam (1962-64)** producing the CVC; **ARC-I (1966-70, Morarji Desai then K. Hanumanthaiah)** with **20 reports**; **2nd ARC (2005-09, Veerappa Moily)** with **15 reports** — the master reference.

Know at least five by name and number: **1st RTI**, **4th Ethics in Governance**, **5th Public Order**, **10th Refurbishing of Personnel Administration**, **11th Promoting e-Governance**, **12th Citizen Centric Administration**, **13th Organisational Structure of Government of India**, **15th State and District Administration**.

items.t: The signature argument on Indian reform
items.d: **India reformed processes, not structures.** Every demonstrable gain since 2005 — **RTI, DBT, UPI, GeM, PFMS, faceless assessment** — came from **re-engineering transactions**. Every **structural** recommendation — the **three-level secretariat**, **executive agencies**, a **Public Services Bill**, a **Fiscal Council**, a **multi-member CAG** — remains unimplemented.

items.t: Why structural reform fails and process reform succeeds
items.d: Process reform is **technocratic**: it can be done by executive order, shows measurable results within a term, and **creates no identifiable loser at the top**. Structural reform **redistributes authority** — it needs legislation, federal consent, and asks the political executive to give up **the discretion it most values**.

**2024 Q6(a).** True, but say something more precise. **Political will is not a personal virtue** — it is produced when the **political cost of not reforming exceeds the cost of reforming**. Reform succeeds where a **crisis, a court order, a fiscal constraint or an electoral incentive** creates that arithmetic: **GST, IBC, RTI, Aadhaar**.

The standing obstacles: **federal division** — most administrative subjects are with the States; **service rules and Article 311** making personnel change slow; **fiscal cost** of any restructuring; **no owner** once the commission dissolves; and **no implementation tracking** — India has no standing body reporting on which recommendations were accepted and acted on.

items.t: What a serious reform agenda would contain
items.d: Close with these five: a **Public Services Bill** codifying values and tenure; a **three-level secretariat** with the **desk officer system**; **independent evaluation with sunset clauses** on schemes; a **National Tribunals Commission**; and **fiscal empowerment of the third tier**. Each has an authoritative recommendation behind it and none needs a new idea.
